In [[Euclidean geometry]], the '''Vecten points''' are two [[triangle center]]s, points associated with any [[triangle]]. They may be found by constructing three [[square]]s on the sides of the triangle, connecting each square centre by a line to the opposite triangle point, and finding the point where these three lines meet. The outer and inner Vecten points differ according to whether the squares are extended outward from the triangle sides, or inward.

The Vecten points are named after an early 19th-century French mathematician named Vecten, who taught mathematics with [[Joseph Diaz Gergonne|Gergonne]] in [[Nîmes]] and published a study of the figure of three squares on the sides of a triangle in 1817.<ref>{{citation|first=Jean-Louis|last=Ayme|title=La Figure de Vecten|url=http://jl.ayme.pagesperso-orange.fr/Docs/La%20figure%20de%20Vecten.pdf|access-date=2026-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231002164922/http://jl.ayme.pagesperso-orange.fr/Docs/La%20figure%20de%20Vecten.pdf|archive-date=2023-10-02}}.</ref>

==Outer Vecten point==

Let {{math|△''ABC''}} be any given [[Plane (geometry)|plane]] [[triangle]]. On the sides {{mvar|BC, CA, AB}} of the triangle, construct outwardly drawn three squares  with centres {{mvar|O{{sub|a}}, O{{sub|b}}, O{{sub|c}}}} respectively. Then the lines {{mvar|AO{{sub|a}}, BO{{sub|b}}, CO{{sub|c}}}} are concurrent. The point of concurrence is the outer Vecten point of {{math|△''ABC''}}.

In [[Clark Kimberling]]'s [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]], the outer Vecten point is denoted by ''X''(485).<ref name=ETC>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers|url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html#X485}}</ref>

[[Isogonal conjugate]] of outer Vecten point is {{Interlanguage link|Kenmotu point|lt=|ja|剣持点}}.<ref name="ETC" />

==Inner Vecten point==

Let {{math|△''ABC''}} be any given [[Plane (geometry)|plane]] [[triangle]]. On the sides {{mvar|BC, CA, AB}} of the triangle, construct inwardly  drawn three squares respectively with centres {{mvar|I{{sub|a}}, I{{sub|b}}, I{{sub|c}}}} respectively. Then the lines {{mvar|AI{{sub|a}}, BI{{sub|b}}, CI{{sub|c}}}} are concurrent. The point of concurrence is the inner Vecten point of {{math|△''ABC''}}.

In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the inner Vecten point is denoted by ''X''(486).<ref name=ETC/>

The line {{math|''X''{{sub|485}}''X''{{sub|486}}}} meets the [[Euler line]] at the [[nine-point center]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}. The Vecten points lie on the [[Kiepert hyperbola]].

==See also==
* [[Napoleon points]], a pair of triangle centers constructed in an analogous way using equilateral triangles instead of squares
